contributions.original_prompts:
New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-payment-intents-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-payment-intents-api-2025.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-payment-intents.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-intents`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-intents the November capture recommends Checkout Sessions with the Payment Element for most integrations, including Adaptive Pricing, while documenting the lower-level Payment Intents flow for complex checkout. A PaymentIntent typically tracks one cart or customer session and can trigger additional authentication. Create it on the server with amount and currency, store its ID so a resumed checkout can reuse it, and use a cart- or session-based idempotency key to avoid duplicate creation. Confirmation attempts payment and can lead to additional action or delayed processing. Retries can produce multiple associated Charge records, with at most one successful Charge per PaymentIntent as described by the separate November API reference. Monitor completion or failure with server webhooks (new raw lines 9-47 and 103-107). Give the corresponding customer the intent's client secret through a TLS-protected SPA endpoint or rendered checkout form. It can complete payment for that amount. Keep it out of logs and merchant-built URLs (new raw lines 49-101). A SetupIntent establishes future payment credentials without a charge. A Checkout Session in elements mode initializes a different checkout SDK from its Session secret and has distinct React and HTML confirmation paths. For a PaymentIntent, setup_future_usage distinguishes customer-present only from off-session or both. The card issuer can still reject a later payment or require authentication (new raw lines 9-26 and 109-131). The April 19 capture establishes the same main sequence and risks (old raw lines 8-48, 50-131 and 133-159). source-stripe-payment-intents.md aggregates five authorities and captures the Checkout preference, but its 'server-only' client-secret shorthand and immediate charge or 3DS-only state claims need correction. Creating or confirming either intent, or seeing a client return, gives no proof of completed payment.
reviewed_answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-intents, the captures establish no substantive PaymentIntent contract change. The November guide adds a coding-agent sandbox paragraph and changes the name in its Radar metadata guidance, from Radar for Fraud Teams to Radar Plus. Neither establishes a PaymentIntent prerequisite, product rename date or plan eligibility. The separate November CLI reference documents the create operation with temporary test credentials for logged-out use, supplied email or Git identity, seven-day expiration and different logged-in behavior. It does not document provisioning through a help flag (old raw lines 8-10 and 184-194, and new raw lines 9-13 and 151-171). Node to curl, Express to Ruby/ERB, formatting and the quickstart and lifecycle links mainly change examples and navigation (old raw lines 25-40 and 58-125, new raw lines 28-39 and 57-101). Keep all April 19 evidence in source-stripe-payment-intents.md, including the other separately sourced lifecycle, status, SetupIntents and async-capture claims. Qualify the reciprocal Payment Intents and Checkout routes so Checkout Elements' Session secret and versioned UI initialization are distinguishable from PaymentIntent client-secret delivery and client confirmation. The intent secret goes only to the customer under TLS and stays out of logs or merchant-built URLs. The April quickstart's Stripe.js-appended return parameter serves status display, not fulfillment. The broad duplicate-charge wording is scoped to one successful Charge per intent and is compatible with multiple attempts. Idempotency remains explicit. The separate November cancel reference lines 7-11 documents direct cancellation of a Checkout Session's PaymentIntent in requires_capture only. Otherwise expire the Checkout Session. Both captures' descriptor lead-in conflicts with their note and the Create reference: card charges use statement_descriptor_suffix and non-card charges use statement_descriptor. Preserve the original note and both dated examples (old raw lines 42-48, 125-131 and 161-182, new raw lines 41-47, 101-107 and 133-149). The dated April 19 statement-descriptor and metadata Create examples write payment_method_types (old raw lines 165-176 and 196-209). November's examples omit it without naming an API version or reason (new raw lines 137-143 and 163-169). Separately, the November-captured Endive changelog lines 5-36 records HTTP 400 with payment_method_types_no_longer_supported on the linked 2026-09-30.endive PaymentIntent Create endpoint, preserves the read-only object property and also names 2026-08-26.preview in its Impact section. Keep the April examples dated and link the REST warning alongside the exact-version stripe@23.0.0 SDK warning in the Payment Intents concept. The April and November lifecycle captures both use simplified 3DS-and-mandate phrasing. Correct source lines 22 and 61 with the separately bundled April 19 Setup Intents guide at lines 28-50 and 52-68. Applicable authentication such as 3DS is distinct from explicit consent to save for on-session use and the upfront customer agreement for off-session charging. 3DS alone gives neither mandate consent nor a guaranteed later SCA exemption. SetupIntent usage describes future use in the setup flow without charging. PaymentIntent setup_future_usage describes intended reuse with a payment (old raw lines 133-159 and new raw lines 109-131). The issuer may still reject a later payment or require authentication. Metadata is copied on Charge creation and later intent edits do not update old Charges. Keep sensitive data out of metadata and description (old raw lines 184-211 and new raw lines 151-171).

Source line 84 compresses all three fields into a single rule and hides the expanded-field case, webhook destination-charge example and API version boundary. `balance_transaction` applies for asynchronous-capture Charges generally, while `transfer` and `application_fee` are Connect-related. Their appearance in `charge.updated` is specifically annotated for destination charges, rather than a universal Connect charge expectation (new lines 40-61, 84-108; old lines 32-52, 74-97).

Source lines 17 and 22 say PaymentIntent creates an immediate charge without adequate qualification. Source lines 24 and 35 describe manual authorization/capture and asynchronous payment-method states. Preserve them as distinct from `automatic_async`, which can show `PaymentIntent.status=succeeded`, `Charge.captured=true` and a null balance transaction together (new lines 40-76). Response, status and bookkeeping availability do not by themselves establish payout or availability of funds for payout.

Root index line 7 routes via Stripe index lines 23 and 729 to `wiki/concepts/stripe-payment-intents.md`. Its core flow at lines 50-55 and source routes at 134-142 lack a reciprocal async-capture reference.

substantive_changes: New lines 11-17 explicitly cover expanded `balance_transaction` and `latest_charge.balance_transaction` unavailability and make handling missing balance data mandatory. The old guide showed nulls and recommended later events without addressing these explicit expansion requests (old lines 30-52, 68-76). This is added operational guidance, not a newly observed API behavior.

Old raw line 74 displayed `charge.updated` but targeted `charge.created`. New raw line 84 corrects the destination to `charge.updated`, a material navigation correction affecting which event an integrator discovers. The intended event was already evident from old SLA and payload headings (old 68-86); no webhook rename occurred.
historical_claims_to_preserve: April describes faster responses with capture completed in the background and points to explicit `automatic_async` on creation, including create-and-confirm in the example. The standalone opening mentions confirmation (old lines 8-12 and 20-27), but does not by itself establish any confirm-endpoint schema. November centers creation (new 19-36).

conflicts: Old event link text and href conflict (old line 74); new line 84 aligns them. Preserve old provenance and warn readers opening the old raw to follow `charge.updated`, not `charge.created`.

New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-payment-intents-asynchronous-capture-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-async-capture-2025.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-payment-intents.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-intents/asynchronous-capture`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: The November 7, 2026 guide at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-intents/asynchronous-capture says `automatic_async` during PaymentIntent creation allows faster confirmation by completing capture in the background. The captured guide calls it the latest API default, so explicit selection is optional there (new raw lines 9-36 and old raw lines 8-28). The pictured succeeded PaymentIntent and captured Charge can precede Charge `balance_transaction` availability even when expanded. The initial attached Charge in the API response and the `charge.succeeded` and `payment_intent.succeeded` events can lack that data. Connect transfer and application fee data may also be deferred, with the later `charge.updated` sample annotating these two fields for destination charges. The example PaymentIntent response and webhook `latest_charge` shape is scoped to version 2022-11-15 or later (new raw lines 38-76 and new raw lines 90-108). Use `charge.updated` for balance transaction and `application_fee.created` and `transfer.created` for applicable Connect objects. The one-hour SLA is for `charge.updated` after successful confirmation (new raw lines 78-86 and old raw lines 68-97). source-stripe-payment-intents.md names the core events but compresses field and version qualifications. Faster response and populated ledger fields are separate, and neither establishes payout.
reviewed_answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-intents/asynchronous-capture, November adds explicit nullable expansion-handling instructions and fixes the old `charge.updated` text pointing to `charge.created` (old raw lines 30-52, old raw lines 68-81, new raw lines 11-17 and new raw lines 78-86). This updates integration guidance and navigation without proving a new event or capture transition. The Node-to-cURL example change, example `return_url` and reformatted payloads do not establish new API/SDK requirements (old raw lines 14-28 and new raw lines 25-36). The April opening says to set `capture_method=automatic_async` when confirming (old raw line 8), while the opt-in text and example put the parameter on PaymentIntent creation with `confirm=true` (old raw lines 10-28). November likewise puts it on creation, including the form-encoded `POST /v1/payment_intents` create-and-confirm example (new raw lines 19-36). These captures do not establish support for the parameter on the standalone confirm endpoint or prove its removal. Keep the dated older evidence in source-stripe-payment-intents.md, route to the corrected event, and distinguish latest-API default wording, the separate `2024-04-10` creation-default changelog, and 2022-11-15-or-later sample response coverage (old raw lines 54-66 and new raw lines 63-76). Warn that manual capture and delayed payment-method processing are separate from asynchronous background capture, and that the one-hour availability SLA is stated only for `charge.updated` after successful confirmation (old raw lines 68-76 and new raw lines 78-108). Connect fee/transfer field availability, funds availability, settlement and payout have separate boundaries.
